explanation: The agent correctly resolved “the ending” to seconds five through eight and preserved the opening with a trim. However, video-edit had no working endpoint, so it produced no edited ending; assembly then received only the five-second opening and delivered an incomplete video.
better_chain: trim (preserve the original first five seconds unchanged) → frame (extract the original frame at the five-second boundary) → image-edit (add an open blank notebook on the desk while preserving the plane, camera, lighting, and animation style) → image-to-video (animate a three-second continuation in which the same plane lands and rests on the notebook; discard audio) → assemble (join the untouched five-second opening and three-second ending into one silent eight-second 16:9 video) → gate (verify duration, silent audio, continuity, no text, and the completed notebook landing)

steps.issue: A newly described animated scene is a suitable use of text-to-video. The prompt specifies the glide and landing timing, eight-second duration, widescreen aspect, no text, and discarded audio.
Trimming seconds zero through five preserves the requested opening without regeneration.
Trimming seconds five through eight correctly isolates the segment referred to as the ending.
Video-edit is conceptually appropriate, but its endpoint was not wired and the reported result was only a placeholder. It could not supply the revised three-second ending.
Assembly requires two real clips, but notebook_ending.mp4 was not produced. Proceeding with the missing second input yielded one five-second piece instead of the requested eight-second video.

missing: A working generation path for the revised three-second ending, plus validation that both clips exist and the assembled output is eight seconds long before delivery.
